scenes.text: You probably think that amazing, earthy smell right after it rains is just water hitting dry ground, but the actual truth behind petrichor is actually a little creepy.
When raindrops hit the soil, they trap tiny air bubbles that shoot upwards and burst, launching a massive aerosol spray of a compound called geosmin which is released by dying bacteria.
Humans are incredibly sensitive to this bacterial compound, possessing an evolutionary ability to detect it in the air far better than a shark can sense blood in the ocean.
Your brain evolved to love this smell because it pointed our ancient ancestors toward water and survival, so tell me in the comments, did I just completely ruin rainy days for you?
